real_qa.q: What are the top 10 most common mistakes employers make when terminating employees?
real_qa.r: The top 10 preventable mistakes include: failing to document every problem, ignoring your own handbook policies, treating employees differently, terminating after a protected activity such as requesting leave or reporting harassment, holding unemotional and professional termination meetings, failing to investigate complaints before terminating, withholding wages without proper justification, failing to recover company property, not providing separation notice in writing, and failing to consult with legal counsel before termination.

real_qa.q: What must an employee manual include to provide legal defense in termination disputes?
real_qa.r: An employee manual should comprehensively cover Title VII discrimination protections, ADA accommodations procedures, Family Medical Leave Act requirements, OSHA safety protocols, Fair Labor Standards Act wage and hour rules, attendance policies, PTO policies, anti-harassment policies both sexual and non-sexual, NDA requirements, social media and internet policies, technology and AI utilization guidelines, progressive discipline procedures, and a clear complaint process. The manual should be 80 to 100 pages covering all these essentials, as it serves as your strongest legal defense in any employment litigation.
real_qa.requete: employee handbook requirements termination legal defense

real_qa.q: What must be included in a separation letter when an employee is terminated?
real_qa.r: A separation letter must specify the final day of employment, final compensation amount, status of all benefits including PTO accrual, COBRA eligibility, 401k information, detailed requirements for equipment return including keys, computers, tablets, and phones with specific timeframes of 24 to 48 hours, clarification that the employee cannot access company systems or facilities after termination, confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations, and any restrictive covenants or non-compete agreements applicable by state law.

real_qa.q: What are the federal laws employers must consider before terminating an employee?
real_qa.r: Employers must consider Title VII which prohibits discrimination based on race, color, creed, sex, origin, or pregnancy; the America with Disabilities Act which requires reasonable accommodation requests be handled interactively with three possible outcomes: grant, modify, or deny; the Family Medical Leave Act for employers with 50 or more employees; the Age Discrimination in Employment Act which provides protected class status for employees over 40 with different release and severance requirements; and OSHA which protects employees reporting safety violations and prohibits retaliation for such reports.
real_qa.requete: federal employment laws termination Title VII ADA FMLA

real_qa.q: What types of retaliation are prohibited when employees report complaints or safety issues?
real_qa.r: Employers absolutely cannot retaliate against employees for reporting harassment claims, filing workers compensation claims, requesting medical leave, complaining about wages, or reporting OSHA safety violations. Retaliation for wrongful termination claims is described as probably one of the biggest and fastest areas for litigation. If federal agencies like OSHA audit your business regarding a termination following an employee complaint, it creates significant legal exposure. Every business should have a process for reporting harassment and anti-retaliation policies in their employee handbooks.
real_qa.requete: retaliation prohibited employee complaints workers compensation OSHA

real_qa.q: What specific documentation and procedures must employers follow for reasonable accommodation requests under the ADA?
real_qa.r: When an employee requests a medical accommodation, employers must have a written accommodation procedure in place. The request should document the medical reasons for the accommodation in writing, and the employer must engage in an interactive process with only three possible outcomes: grant the accommodation, modify it, or deny it with specific justification. Employers cannot discriminate based on disability, and failure to consider reasonable accommodation requests in compliance with federal guidelines creates significant liability with federal authorities.
real_qa.requete: ADA reasonable accommodation request interactive process documentation
